title: Integrability from bounded pairings
statement:
Let $(\alpha,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $q>1$, and let $u:\alpha\to\mathbb R$ be integrable. Suppose $C\ge0$ and, for every essentially bounded measurable $g:\alpha\to\mathbb R$, 
\[\left|\int u g\,d\mu\right|\le C\,\|g\|_{q/(q-1)},\]
where the norm is the extended $L^{q/(q-1)}$ norm converted to a real number. Then $u$ belongs to $L^q(\mu)$ and its extended $L^q$ norm is at most $C$.
hypotheses_covered: $\mu$ is a probability measure on a measurable space
The pairing inequality holds for every essentially bounded measurable real-valued $g$, with the stated $L^{q/(q-1)}$ norm bound
